title: The Off-Season Revenue Problem: How Lucknow Super Giants Can Stay Relevant Year-Round
dek: Lucknow Super Giants play for a couple of months and then go quiet. The calendar shows how long the off-season is, and why staying relevant is a year-round job.
excerpt: On average Lucknow Super Giants go most of the year between matches. Every revenue line has to survive that gap.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: Lucknow Super Giants' season has lasted {{ev:os-active}} days on average, first match to last.
The gap to the next season's first match has averaged {{ev:os-gap}} days.
That leaves {{ev:os-share}} of each cycle without a LSG match.

sections.heading: A Short Season, a Long Silence
body: From Lucknow Super Giants' first match to their last, a season has lasted {{ev:os-active}} days on average. The wait for the next season's first match has averaged {{ev:os-gap}} days.
That leaves {{ev:os-share}} of each cycle with no LSG cricket at all: the off-season revenue problem in one number.

sections.heading: What Fills the Gap
body: Off-season attention comes from retention decisions, the auction, players' international and domestic cricket, and the franchise's own content.
Each of those is a chance to keep fans engaged, but only the auction is guaranteed every year.

sections.heading: Revenue Without Matches
body: Year-round revenue ideas include academies, membership programmes, archive content and events.

sections.heading: What the Warehouse Cannot See
body: The CricField warehouse is ball-by-ball cricket data. It contains no off-season revenue, engagement or membership data, so it cannot measure the commercial side of this question directly.
Measuring the problem directly would need monthly revenue and engagement figures across a full year.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Plan for the Silence
body: Lucknow Super Giants spend most of each year without matches. Off-season planning should be as deliberate as squad planning.
The archive of moments and the auction are the most dependable off-season stories.

methodology: CricField measures the cricket a franchise puts on the field; it holds no revenue, attendance, audience, merchandise or social-media data. Season length = days from the franchise's first to last match; off-season = days to the next season's first match.
